headline: Computational methods correct spatial RNA leakage and infer single-cell states
label: Computational Spatial Transcriptomics Frameworks
summary: Recent preprints and publications pair spatial decontamination, uncertainty-aware modeling and single-cell network inference with rigorous benchmarking.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational recovery of cell-level and spatial structure from noisy or aggregated measurements. SPARKLE and CLEAR-ST both correct local RNA leakage in high-resolution spatial transcriptomics, the former via out-of-mask spatial evidence and the latter through a physics-informed model of mRNA lateral diffusion. HIDE-Deconv estimates cell-type compositions jointly across a hierarchy of resolutions, and bulk2scDiff generates single-cell expression profiles conditioned on pseudobulk input. Clustering and evaluation work, including ClustoCell benchmarked across 450 datasets and the SACCELERATOR consensus workflow for spatially aware clustering, addresses how partitions are defined and assessed. What is new is explicit probabilistic or hierarchical modeling of contamination, composition and uncertainty, applied to spatial as well as single-cell data. Not every item shares this focus; the metabolic modeling and disease-classification work extend the toolkit more broadly.
